name: Bolton

licensing.selective: No selective licensing scheme in force (an earlier scheme in Tonge Moor began in 2008 and ran for five years).
licensing.additional: Borough-wide additional HMO licensing agreed by the Cabinet in August 2026 (covering smaller HMOs of three or four people and some converted buildings), expected to be fully running in early 2027; until then only national mandatory HMO licensing applies. An Article 4 direction since 2025 means small HMO conversions need planning permission.
licensing.fee: £1,211 per property for a five-year licence under the planned additional HMO scheme

rent.text: £883 a month (ONS, May 2026), up 9.8% on a year earlier

price.text: £200,000 (UK HPI, April 2026, provisional), up about 1.9% on a year earlier

councilTax.text: £2,392 Band D (2026/27) outside parished areas, including the police and Greater Manchester mayoral (fire) precepts; about £2,400 on average with parish precepts

housing: Bolton's housing is dominated by Victorian brick terraces built for the cotton mills, especially in the inner areas around Deane, Daubhill and Great Lever, where private renting is common. The University of Bolton brings some student lets close to the town centre. Farnworth, Kearsley and Little Lever have similar terraced streets and post-war estates, while Horwich and Westhoughton have grown with large new-build estates. The north of the borough, around Turton, is mostly owner-occupied with stone villages on the moors.
checkinTips: Victorian terraces in Deane, Daubhill and Great Lever: photograph damp at the base of walls, cellar heads and mould in back bedrooms and bathrooms.
Back yards and ginnels behind terraced rows: record the yard gate, walls and where the bins are kept.
Student lets near the University of Bolton: photograph each bedroom lock, fire doors and alarms, and the shared kitchen separately.
Mill conversions and town-centre flats: note fob and key counts, the intercom and any parking space or bike store.
New-build estates in Horwich and Westhoughton: record snagging marks, sealant and new gardens and fences.
Stone cottages in the Turton moorland villages: photograph stoves, any oil or LPG supply and exposed walls and windows.
tenantHelp: Tenants can report disrepair, damp or unsafe conditions in privately rented homes to Bolton Council's private sector housing team.
